subject: Private offer pricing for Azure + GCP: banded tiers, reseller overage handling
messages:
From: Sara Cho <sara.cho@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer pricing for Azure + GCP: banded tiers, reseller overage handling

Hi Evelyn / Ben / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's performance on 8k context workloads. We're ready to move to a private offer but have a few pricing/packaging questions we need clarified before procurement will sign: 

1) Banding logic: we have two major product SKUs (S1: baseline inference, S2: high-throughput GPU). Does Redwood support a single private-offer price with usage bands (e.g., $X per token up to band A, $Y per token in band B) across both Azure and GCP marketplaces, or do you recommend separate PO rows per cloud?

2) Channel margin / reseller pass-through: Our reseller (Nimbus Resell) expects a consistent gross margin on resold private offers. Can Redwood set a pass-through margin of 16% on list price in the private offer, or do we need to bake it into the list price and use a separate reseller rebate flow?

3) Overage and burst handling: We plan to commit to a monthly baseline (committed sum) but need predictable caps for bursts. How are overage tokens invoiced in marketplace POs (immediate overage at list, or weekly true-up)? Any options for capping overage or pre-authorized burst buckets?

4) Procurement items: Are there recommended PO language snippets for tax/treatment and for the reseller margin flow? We frequently need example contract lines for our internal procurement to slot into the PO.

Would appreciate a quick call if this is easier — procurement is pushing for answers this week. I'm copying procurement directly in case they want to chime in.

Thanks,
Sara Cho
Head of Platform Partnerships
Acme Analytics

Attachments: acme-security-req.pdf (see last message)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer pricing for Azure + GCP: banded tiers, reseller overage handling

Sara — thanks, great questions. I put a short matrix together that should answer most of this; attaching the pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx). Summary answers below to keep the thread tidy.

Quick answers:
- Banding across clouds: We can support banded pricing in a single private-offer if the SKU mapping is identical across clouds. Where SKU names/units differ (Azure CSP SKU vs GCP listing), we recommend separate PO rows per cloud to avoid reconciliation drift. In practice, many customers prefer separate rows for Azure and GCP so the accounting team can match marketplace invoices directly.

- Channel margin: Redwood can either:
  1) Support a listed "reseller discount" field in the private offer (pass-through) — Nimbus would see a 16% pass-through automatically, but that requires marketplace support on the reseller side (GCP/AWS support this pattern; Azure has more variability depending on the distributor). OR
  2) Bake margin into the list price and issue post-billing rebates to the reseller (more universally compatible).

- Overage and bursts: Marketplace invoicing is typically monthly true-up. We can configure a pre-authorized burst bucket (e.g., additional monthly bucket of N tokens) that is billed only if used; otherwise unused burst is not billed. We can also apply a hard cap; if you hit the cap, requests will receive throttled 429s.

- PO language: See the sample snippets in the attached workbook. High-level: call out committed usage, per-token overage rate, reseller pass-through vs rebate approach, and explicit tax/responsibility lines.

If helpful, Ben and Lauren and I can hop on a 30-min call today to walk procurement through the worksheet. Proposed times: 2:00pm or 4:00pm PT.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
VP Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (pricing band examples + procurement snippets)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer pricing for Azure + GCP: banded tiers, reseller overage handling

Eve / Lauren — internal note before we finalize the sheet to send Sara / procurement. I've sketched margin/pass-through ops below and a recommended default:

- Recommended default: Separate PO rows per cloud (cleaner for Acme accounting) + list price that already reflects the reseller gross margin (so Nimbus gets predictable margin without requiring their marketplaces to support pass-through). That will avoid reconciliation friction.

- Band thresholds suggestion (example):
  * Band A: 0 - 250M tokens/month -> $0.0009/token
  * Band B: 250M - 1B tokens/month -> $0.00075/token
  * Band C: >1B tokens/month -> $0.00060/token
  These are placeholder numbers; final prices in the sheet.

- Overage handling: Recommend a pre-authorized burst bucket (we'll set at 20% of committed for launch) plus monthly true-up at the Band A rate unless they cross into higher bands. Hard cap only on explicit ask.

- Tax/treatment: call out that marketplace invoice may include applicable VAT/GST by the marketplace; Redwood's PO language will indicate whether Redwood or buyer is responsible for withholding. Procurement often wants the line 'Buyer is responsible for any local indirect taxes unless otherwise stated.'

I'll review the spreadsheet and propose final numbers by EOD. If Eve wants me to join the call today, I'm available at 4:00pm PT.

—Ben
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer pricing for Azure + GCP: banded tiers, reseller overage handling

Sara — following up with the formal proposal and the attached worksheet (same file) with suggested list prices and the reseller-friendly flow we discussed. Key points for procurement: 

- We've prepared two PO variants attached to the worksheet: (A) Separate-cloud PO rows with list prices that include a 16% reseller margin; (B) Single PO with explicit reseller pass-through (note: GCP/AWS workable, Azure may require distributor confirmation).

- Overage: default is monthly true-up + pre-authorized burst bucket equal to 20% of committed volume. We can lower or remove burst on request.

- Example procurement language (copy/paste):
  "Seller will deliver services pursuant to the Marketplace Order. Buyer will be invoiced monthly for committed usage and any overage at the rates specified in the Order. Any reseller discounts or rebates described in the Order shall be paid by Seller to the designated reseller within 30 days post-invoice reconciliation, subject to Buyer verifying reseller entitlement."

- Next steps: If variant A (list price includes reseller margin) works for Acme, procurement can issue an initial PO referencing "RDW-ACME-202705-A" and we'll create the private offer in Azure and GCP. If variant B is required, we need a quick call with Nimbus to confirm pass-through compatibility on Azure.

I pasted the hubspot deal link here for reference: https://hubspot.com/deals/ACME-9273.

Would Monday be OK to target a signed PO? Happy to jump on a call with procurement if they want to review line-by-line.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Revenue Operations Manager

Lauren — thanks for the clear options and the worksheet. Procurement is fine with Variant A (list price includes reseller margin) — simpler for our finance team. They asked me to confirm two operational items before issuing PO: 

1) Can you confirm the marketplace invoice will include an itemized line for committed vs overage usage? They need that to map to their GL.
2) For Azure specifically, can Redwood confirm the private offer will be visible to Nimbus Resell (our distributor) so they can reconcile their commission? If not, we'll attach a short reseller-side addendum.

I've attached our security checklist for reference (acme-security-req.pdf). Procurement will be on a short call Monday at 11:00am ET to sign off and issue PO if both items are cleared.
